column1: # Blueforce Field OS - SBOM / package lock schema for the offline APT bundle
# build-offline-repo.sh writes this layout into a built bundle as:
#     <output>/packages.lock.tsv
# scripts/install/blueforce-install.sh validates that file before any package
# module runs: it must exist, be non-empty, carry the header on the FIRST line
# byte for byte, and every row must hold a package, a version, an architecture,
# a 64-character lower-case sha256, and the pool file name of the .deb.
# Columns (TAB-separated, exactly five, header first):
#   package        lower-case Debian package name      ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9+.-]*$
#   version        exact Debian version, epochs allowed
#   architecture   binary architecture                e.g. amd64, all
#   sha256         sha256sum of the .deb, 64 lower-case hex characters
#   source         file name of the .deb inside <output>/pool/
# LAB fill procedure:
#   1. review the .deb files and place them in one local pool directory
#   2. fill every UNPINNED version in manifests/*.txt from those .deb files
#   3. ./build-offline-repo.sh --packages /secure/reviewed-debs --output /srv/blueforce-apt
#   4. the released packages.lock.tsv is the build output; never hand-edit a
#      released lock, and never hand-write a sha256 - the build recomputes it
# This template is documentation, not a bundle artifact: the header sits below the
# comments so the file can never be mistaken for a released packages.lock.tsv.
# ==== EXAMPLE ROWS - format illustration only, never a released artifact ====
# <package>
